## Summary

**The attended CLI lifecycle is full form.** `run inspect <run_id>
[view]` attaches read-only and projects any of
`context_view`/`run_summary`/`checkpoint`/`compact`, bounded by
`--until-seq` (declared flag; `--at-seq` alias; a non-integer is a
typed `invocation_error` before any kernel call — ADR-0274 D1).
`run resume` takes `--mode continue|takeover`/`--takeover`, runs the
attended loop under `--follow`, preserves the writer session without
it, and surfaces `resume_checkpoint_unavailable` verbatim while
DF-S1.25-2 stands. `run fork` requires exactly one of
`--at-seq`/`--at-event` and preserves the parent writer. `run cancel`
distinguishes run-scope (closes on completion, `cancelled` exit class)
from `--turn` scope (no second cancel minted).

**Reader-set withholding reaches the output boundary** — the
DF-S2.10-2 half of AC-R-2.11.1-16, now closed. `emit_result` (`json`)
and `render_event` (`jsonl`) pass every record through
`withhold_uncovered(doc, io.principal)`: a `content`-class item whose
`readers`/`provenance.readers` set does not cover the invocation
principal loses `content`/`payload` to the typed tombstone
`{withheld:{reason:"reader_set_uncovered"}}`; `seq`/`class`/
`authority`/`readers` stay visible, `public`/absent never withhold,
nested structures recurse. `run start --jsonl`/`run events` share the
seam, so O-1 byte-parity holds *with* tombstones applied. The LT
battery over the gate (`lt_battery_no_secret_bytes_through_the_gate`)
shows no planted secret byte string survives.

**Registry enforcement is landed.** `StaleIndex` propagates
transitively: `Lineage::revoke` marks dependants
`stale_by_dependency` (BFS over the dependency map), and declaring a
dependency on an already-revoked member is stale at declare time —
revocation is a record, not a flag. `deprecate`/`yank`/`revoke` are
real registry ops; execute-mode resolution refuses revoked/yanked
heads. `record_conformance` requires durable runs (`RunNotDurable`
typed) and folds conformance-derived stale into floor/vector results;
`catalog(filter)`, `sameness(a,b)` (the L0–L4 ladder),
`update_available`, `slot_choices`, `query` land alongside the
widening-extension path (budget loosening via `declared_costs`,
extension requests/hook growth) with `diff_ref` computed, persisted,
and verified — widening bumps the label to MAJOR.
`EnvironmentRecord` is a first-class kind (`idp("environment")`
digest) across records/kinds/schema/identity.

**The invariant holds and is tested:** *a revoked memory is never
returned under default validity* — the S-106 regression shows a
revoked candidate outranking its replacement pre-filter, withheld by
validity, the replacement served; `Audit` mode returns it annotated.

**Group L `lab.registry.*` dispatch** routes all 17 declared ops
through `RegistryStore` in `hh-embed/src/registry_ops.rs`, under the
declared gate order (hello → init → op lookup → upcall rejection →
experimental → `serves_measurement` capability → implementation gate →
dispatch) with durable mutations on the single fenced ledger writer
(ADR-0274 D6). Schema artifacts regenerated via `hh-codegen` (CC7).

**`ModelSnapshotRecord` + the fingerprint probe** (R-2.3.4, §5b.4):
`hh-gateway/src/snapshot.rs` carries the record `{provider, model_id,
snapshot_id?, pinned, provenance = reported, observed_fingerprint?}`
as `RecordKind::ModelSnapshot` — `version_id` over the full record
under `model_snapshot`, `semantic_id` the `{provider, model_id}`
projection (a snapshot roll is a new version of the same line —
ADR-0274 D3). `dependency_stamp() == version_id()`, so any observed
change is a new stamp for `stale_by_dependency`. The probe is the
declared canonical request `hh.fingerprint/v1`; the observed
fingerprint is the `idp/1` digest under `model_snapshot.fingerprint`;
the verdict is closed `{match, drift, unknown}` — absence is never
drift. `observe()` folds served fields against the pin and raises the
synthetic `SnapshotClaim` (`snapshot_id = observed`) on served-model
substitution *or* fingerprint drift — the gateway reports, the
router/registry owns the consequence (I-NOAUTH; ADR-0203 D5;
ADR-0274 D5).
